question: What does the interquartile range measure and how are outlier fences defined?
answer: Outlier fences are defined using the IQR: values below Q1 - 1.5 * IQR or above Q3 + 1.5 * IQR are flagged as outliers. [S1]

citations.title: Statistics Lecture Notes
citations.text: 1. Descriptive Statistics Descriptive statistics summarize a dataset. Measures of central tendency are the mean (the sum of the values divided by the number of values), the median (the middle value of the sorted data) and the mode (the most frequent value). The mean is sensitive to outliers; the median is robust to them. For right-skewed data such as incomes the mean is usually larger than the median. Measures of spread describe variability. The range is maximum minus minimum. The variance averages squared deviations from the mean, and the standard deviation is the square root of the variance, so it has the same units as the data. The interquartile range (IQR) is Q3 minus Q1 and is used to flag outliers: a common rule marks values below Q1 - 1.5 * IQR or above Q3 + 1.5 * IQR. Population variance divides the sum of squared deviations by N, the population size. Sample

S2.title: Statistics Lecture Notes
S2.text: size grows. A confidence interval gives a range of plausible values for a parameter. A 95% confidence interval for  a mean with known sigma is x-bar plus or minus 1.96 * sigma / sqrt(n). When sigma is unknown and n is small, replace 1.96 with a critical value from the t distribution with n - 1 degrees of freedom. A 95% confidence level means that if the procedure were repeated many times, about 95% of the intervals would contain the true parameter; it does not mean there is a 95% probability that one specific computed interval contains it.

S4.title: Python Reference Notes
S4.text:
BUILT-IN FUNCTIONS
len(x) returns the number of items in x.
sum(nums) adds the numbers in an iterable.
min(nums) and max(nums) return the smallest and largest items.
sorted(items) returns a new sorted list; list.sort() sorts in place and returns None.
enumerate(items) gives (index, item) pairs.
zip(a, b) pairs items from two iterables and stops at the shortest.
range(stop) generates 0 .. stop-1; range(start, stop, step) supports steps.
isinstance(x, int) tests whether x is an instance of a type.

S6.title: Statistics Reference Notes
S6.text:
DESCRIPTIVE FORMULAS
Mean: x-bar = (sum of x) / n
Population variance: sigma^2 = sum((x - mu)^2) / N
Sample variance: s^2 = sum((x - x-bar)^2) / (n - 1)
Standard deviation: the square root of the variance.
IQR = Q3 - Q1. Outlier fences: Q1 - 1.5*IQR and Q3 + 1.5*IQR.
Coefficient of variation: CV = standard deviation / mean.

Exercise C2. Write a safe_divide(a, b) function that returns None and prints a message when b is zero, using try and except ZeroDivisionError.

S10.title: Statistics Robust Summaries
S10.text:
The mean is the sum of the values divided by their count, so every value, including extreme ones,
pulls it. The median is the middle value of the sorted data and ignores how far the extremes lie.
When a distribution is right-skewed (a long tail of a few very large values, as with prices or
incomes) a few large values drag the mean upward while the median stays near the typical value, so
the mean exceeds the median. When the data are symmetric the two are close. A large gap between the
mean and the median is therefore a quick diagnostic for skew or outliers. For skewed data, report
the median (or both) because it better describes a typical observation.
S10.location: ROBUST SUMMARIES: WHY THE MEAN AND THE MEDIAN DIFFER
